problem: Powerhouse policies required shared context, chat-learning preflight, control-plane binding and universal completion, but a canonical operation binding alone did not prove that the current material run actually executed the latest preflight before mutation.
impact: Chats and agents could appear governed at repository/control-plane level while users observed little behavioral difference, because policy presence and runtime consumption were not the same evidence class.
rootCause: Preflight and completion were independently mandatory contracts without one identity-bound runtime receipt connecting preflight, mutation admission and postflight completion.
failedApproach: Treating broad policy scope, PR-time preflight CI or database operation binding as sufficient proof that every live material execution had consumed current Powerhouse learning.
fix: Use one Powerhouse universal runtime ingress receipt created from the canonical READY chat-learning preflight, bind it to run/actor/candidate identity, require it before Agent Fabric material commands, and require exact run/candidate continuity again at universal completion. The Agent Fabric gateway imports the canonical ingress directly so callers cannot inject an alternate adapter to bypass admission.
prevention: A material Powerhouse-managed execution without a valid ADMITTED ingress receipt is not execution-ready evidence. A terminal completion with another run/candidate receipt is invalid. Read-only queries may remain outside the mutation admission path. Policy presence, CI preflight, operation binding and runtime consumption are separate evidence classes and may never be substituted for each other.

delivery_learning.problem: Opening the delivery PR during the RED/GREEN TDD sequence caused many intermediate commits to trigger the repository-wide workflow set, creating avoidable CI queue and cost noise.
delivery_learning.recovery: The noisy PR #1958 was closed unmerged and replaced by clean verification PR #1959 using the same reviewed candidate lineage. The final protected candidate was merged only after required verification.
delivery_learning.prevention: For broad-workflow repositories, perform bounded RED/GREEN iteration before opening the protected verification PR where safe. Once a verification PR is open, keep one stable candidate SHA; if intermediate-run noise becomes material, preserve exact candidate identity and supersede cleanly rather than creating divergent implementation lineages.
delivery_learning.rule: CI queue pressure is an operational cost signal, not a reason to weaken gates. Reduce redundant runs while preserving exact-head verification and protected merge semantics.

boundary: Repository code cannot alter the native ChatGPT product runtime. The enforceable invariant is that any material Powerhouse mutation invoked from such a chat must cross the managed ingress/control-plane before mutation.
reuse_rule: Future agent/chat runtime work must distinguish policy presence, preflight execution proof, mutation admission proof and terminal completion proof; never infer one from another. Preserve one canonical delivery lineage, minimize redundant CI runs, and never trade exact-head evidence for speed or cost reduction.
